requirements.statement: FDIR converts recorded document-form facts rather than semantic meaning.
The initial capability scope names DOCX, XLSX, PDF, and Markdown explicitly.
The output is a typed, validated, machine-readable Document Form IR.
Structure, presentation, layout, geometry, and order are separate responsibilities.
Semantic interpretation is downstream of Document Form IR.
A format-specific feature may remain an extension without weakening the common core.
Universal means extensible without breaking the common model, not all-format feature completeness.
Every normative term has an observable definition in the product documentation.
The JSON Schema and its generated contract share one normative version.
Generated artifacts are accepted only after deterministic regeneration matches.
Canonical IR JSON is the authority for IR content.
A query index is a rebuildable non-authoritative projection.
Renderer and OCR observations cannot overwrite source-declared facts.
A source map is optional metadata and not an identity authority.
Ingestion metadata is outside the Document Form IR.
Semantic IR may read Document Form facts but cannot redefine their authority.
Document has a stable documentId, sourceFormat, schema reference, root node, and conversion report.
Part represents document sections, pages, sheets, headers, or other bounded areas.
Surface identifies a page, sheet, canvas, or other coordinate-bearing presentation surface.
Node is a closed typed union for structural and visual document elements.
Containment is explicit and cannot be inferred from arbitrary property names.
Text stores source, normalized, displayed, or observed representations as distinct typed values.
TableGrid represents tables, rows, columns, cells, coordinates, and merged regions.
Resource describes an image, chart, font, or object without becoming a source-byte archive.
FormulaField and Annotation are distinct from Text and Node structure.
Every entity defines identity, references, containment, cardinality, and validation invariants.
Core entities use discriminated typed objects rather than a free property bag.
Integer, decimal, boolean, and string are distinct schema types.
Exact decimal values use canonical decimal strings or an explicitly typed decimal pair.
Length carries a numeric value and an explicit unit.
Color supports explicit RGBA and theme-reference variants.
Angles, transforms, and coordinates carry unit and coordinate-space information.
Date and time values keep date-system, locale, timezone, and representation context.
Floating-point observations declare precision and are not used as silent exact-value replacements.
Authored style is represented independently from its resolved display style.
Based-on inheritance is represented as a typed reference.
Theme references are represented independently from direct formatting.
Direct formatting overrides remain observable after style resolution.
Conditional formatting rules remain distinct from computed results.
Font, paragraph, border, fill, stroke, spacing, and visibility use typed fields.
Number format is not stored as a replacement for a cell value.
A style inheritance cycle is rejected with a stable diagnostic.
Every geometry identifies a coordinate space and a unit policy.
Parent coordinate space and transforms are explicit.
Rotation and affine transforms are represented without lossy rectangle flattening.
Points, line segments, polylines, polygons, and bezier paths are typed primitives.
Text baselines and glyph boxes can be represented.
Clipping paths and crop regions can be represented.
Inline, floating, page, sheet, cell, and paragraph anchors are typed variants.
Connector paths, endpoints, arrowheads, and anchor candidates are represented.
Text wrapping and placement constraints are preserved as layout facts.
Z-index and paint order are distinct from document structure order.
Structure, source, reading, drawing, grid, tab, and revision orders are distinct.
A connector target relation does not assert a semantic or causal relationship.
Spreadsheet formulas are separate from stored values.
Cached results are separate from evaluated or displayed values.
Displayed text is separate from raw value type and value.
Calculation context includes formula language, date system, locale, and mode where available.
Word fields preserve instruction and displayed result separately.
PDF character code, glyph, Unicode mapping, and OCR text are separate facts.
Markdown source spelling and normalized/display text are separate representations.
Renderer results do not replace source-declared value fields.
The model supports preserved, normalized, approximated, ambiguous, unsupported, omitted-by-policy, unavailable, and failed.
Document-level status summarizes but does not erase child status.
Feature-level status identifies affected capabilities such as geometry or formulas.
Node-level status identifies a partial or unsupported element.
Field-level status is available when source and display values differ in support.
Diagnostics have stable codes, severity, target, and remediation action.
An unsupported node does not silently disappear from a partial document.
A missing source locator does not invalidate the rest of the IR.
Every extension has namespace, extension type, schema version, and schema identifier.
Every extension payload is validated by a typed extension schema.
Critical and non-critical extension handling is explicit.
Unknown non-critical extensions can be retained without being interpreted.
Unknown critical extensions prevent a complete claim for the affected scope.
Vendor extensions and format extensions use separate namespaces.
Future promotion of an extension to core requires an explicit migration.
Extension compatibility rules distinguish unknown version from invalid payload.
Canonical serialization uses UTF-8, no BOM, and LF line endings.
Canonical object keys and arrays have deterministic ordering.
Canonical decimal formatting is deterministic and does not silently use binary float.
Document identity is derived from canonical IR content, not source bytes.
Schema major and minor compatibility rules are documented and validated.
Migration emits diagnostics for lost, approximated, or ambiguous fields.
Entity IDs are stable under array reordering and absent optional source maps.
Deleting an index does not change canonical IR content or identity.
DOCX document, section, paragraph, run, table, row, and cell map to core nodes.
DOCX styles, themes, inheritance, direct formatting, and resolved style are separate.
DOCX numbering and list levels retain their source order and level context.
DOCX fields, revisions, comments, footnotes, endnotes, links, bookmarks, and controls are distinct annotations.
DOCX drawings, shapes, text boxes, connectors, equations, and anchors map to typed geometry and layout.
DOCX embedded and linked objects use resource descriptions rather than source-byte archives.
DOCX known loss and unsupported features carry stable diagnostics.
DOCX conversion does not claim business meaning for text, red formatting, or connectors.
XLSX workbook, worksheet, row, column, and cell map to core nodes and surfaces.
XLSX shared strings and inline strings retain their representation distinction.
XLSX formula, raw value, stored value, cached result, and displayed text are distinct.
XLSX error values and stale caches remain explicit.
XLSX number formats, date systems, locale, and calculation context are explicit.
XLSX styles, themes, merges, names, tables, validations, and conditional formatting map to typed entities.
XLSX drawings, charts, pivots, cell anchors, and external references are represented or diagnosed.
XLSX conversion does not silently recalculate or replace stored values.
PDF pages and coordinate systems map to Part and Surface entities.
PDF text fragments, character codes, glyphs, fonts, and Unicode mappings are separate.
PDF text matrices and glyph geometry map to affine transforms and boxes.
PDF paths, fills, strokes, images, graphics state, transforms, and clipping are typed.
PDF annotations, forms, outlines, destinations, attachments, and tagged structure are represented or diagnosed.
PDF paint order and reading-order candidates are separate orders.
PDF renderer observations and OCR observations are distinct from source-declared facts.
PDF xref history, unreferenced bytes, and forensic archive evidence are outside the IR core.
Markdown block and inline structure map to typed nodes.
Markdown headings, paragraphs, lists, and tables retain structure and source order.
Markdown links, images, and reference definitions are distinct annotations and resources.
Markdown code blocks, inline code, emphasis, escaping, and entities are represented separately.
Markdown delimiter style and authoring spelling remain available as extension facts.
Markdown raw HTML is preserved as typed extension content without semantic interpretation.
Markdown front matter, footnotes, registered extensions, and line-break policy are explicit.
Markdown dialect normalization and known loss carry diagnostics.
The query layer can list all paragraphs and cells.
The query layer can find formulas and separate displayed from stored values.
The query layer can find resolved red text without asserting what red means.
The query layer can find shapes on a surface and connector target relations.
The query layer can find hidden, unsupported, approximated, and ambiguous nodes.
The query layer can find extensions by namespace and type.
The query layer can traverse Word style inheritance.
The query layer can report PDF glyph and OCR differences without merging them.
Schema tests cover required fields, closed core fields, and typed unions.
Invariant tests cover identity, containment, references, order, and style cycles.
Cross-format tests verify common mappings without semantic equivalence assertions.
Geometry, connector, clipping, and anchor fixtures are executable.
Style inheritance and formula value separation fixtures are executable.
Malformed, partial, unavailable, unsupported, and failed outcomes are tested.
Unknown extension and backward/forward compatibility tests are executable.
Performance and resource limits are tested at the parser and observation boundaries.
